title: Punishments
bareActText: The punishments to which offenders are liable under the provisions of this Sanhita are— (a) Death; (b) Imprisonment for life; (c) Imprisonment, which is of two descriptions, namely:— (1) Rigorous, that is, with hard labour; (2) Simple; (d) Forfeiture of property; (e) Fine; (f) Community service.
plainMeaning: This section is the menu of punishments a court can hand down under BNS. The headline change from the old law is that community service now appears as a recognised punishment in its own right.
ingredients: Punishment must be one of the kinds listed in this section
Imprisonment is either rigorous (with hard labour) or simple
Community service is newly listed as a punishment
punishment: Not applicable — this section defines the kinds of punishment rather than an offence.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds broadly to s.53 IPC; community service is newly added as a listed punishment.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Commutation of sentence
bareActText: The appropriate Government may, without the consent of the offender, commute any punishment under this Sanhita to any other punishment in accordance with section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
plainMeaning: The Government can replace a punishment with a different (lesser) one without needing the offender's agreement, following the procedure in the BNSS. This is the power of commutation.
ingredients: Power lies with the appropriate Government
No consent of the offender is required
Commutation follows the procedure in s.474 BNSS
punishment: Not applicable — this section confers a power to commute, not a punishment.

ipcReference.changeNote: Consolidates the commutation powers previously in ss.54-55 IPC and links them to the BNSS procedure.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Fractions of terms of punishment
bareActText: In calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life shall be reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.
plainMeaning: When a rule needs a fraction of a sentence to be worked out, life imprisonment is treated as twenty years for that calculation.
ingredients: Applies when calculating a fraction of a term
Life imprisonment counts as twenty years for that purpose
punishment: Not applicable — this is a rule of calculation.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.57 IPC; retained without substantive change.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous or simple
bareActText: In every case in which an offender is punishable with imprisonment which may be of either description, it shall be competent to the Court which sentences such offender to direct in the sentence that such imprisonment shall be wholly rigorous, or that such imprisonment shall be wholly simple, or that any part of such imprisonment shall be rigorous and the rest simple.
plainMeaning: Where an offence allows imprisonment 'of either description', the court chooses the mix: all rigorous, all simple, or partly each.
ingredients: The offence must be punishable with imprisonment of either description
The court may direct the imprisonment to be wholly rigorous, wholly simple, or partly each
punishment: Not applicable — this is a sentencing power.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.60 IPC; retained without substantive change.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc.
bareActText: Where no sum is expressed to which a fine may extend, the amount of fine to which the offender is liable is unlimited, but shall not be excessive. Where an offence is punishable with imprisonment as well as fine and the offender is sentenced to a fine (with or without imprisonment), the Court may impose imprisonment in default of payment of the fine, not exceeding one-fourth of the maximum term of imprisonment fixed for the offence. Where the offence is punishable with fine or community service, the simple imprisonment imposed in default shall not exceed: two months where the fine does not exceed five thousand rupees; four months where it does not exceed ten thousand rupees; and one year in any other case. Default imprisonment terminates when the fine is paid or levied, and proportional part-payment reduces it. (Summarised from the section; see the official Act for the full sub-clauses.)
plainMeaning: This section governs fines. When the law fixes no maximum, the fine is unlimited but must not be excessive. It also lets a court order imprisonment if the fine is not paid: where the offence carries imprisonment too, the default term cannot exceed one-fourth of the maximum imprisonment for that offence; where the offence is punishable with fine or community service, the default simple imprisonment is capped at two months (fine up to ₹5,000), four months (up to ₹10,000), or one year (otherwise).
ingredients: Where no maximum is stated, the fine is unlimited but not excessive
The court may set imprisonment in default of paying the fine
If the offence also carries imprisonment: default term ≤ one-fourth of the maximum term for the offence
If punishable with fine/community service: default simple imprisonment ≤ 2 months (≤₹5,000), 4 months (≤₹10,000), or 1 year (otherwise)
Default imprisonment ends if the fine is paid or levied
punishment: Not applicable — this governs fines and default imprisonment rather than defining an offence.

ipcReference.changeNote: Consolidates ss.63-70 IPC into a single section on fines and default imprisonment.

illustrations: If a person is fined and given a default term, paying enough of the fine proportionally shortens or ends the default imprisonment.

verification.source: BNS 2023, s.8 — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
bareActText: Where anything which is an offence is made up of parts, any of which is itself an offence, the offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such his offences, unless it be so expressly provided. (Refer to the Gazette for the full text and related sub-rules on offences falling within several definitions or made up of several offences.)
plainMeaning: If one act is really made up of several smaller offences, the offender is generally not punished separately for each part — only once — unless the law expressly says otherwise.
ingredients: One offence is made up of parts that are themselves offences
Punishment is limited to one of those offences
Unless the law expressly provides for more
punishment: Not applicable — this limits punishment where offences overlap.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.71 IPC on the limit of punishment for compound offences.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
bareActText: In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of which of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided for all. (Refer to the Gazette for the full text.)
plainMeaning: If a court is sure the person committed one of several listed offences but cannot say which, it punishes for the offence carrying the lowest punishment (where the punishments differ).
ingredients: The person is guilty of one of several specified offences
It is doubtful which one
Punishment is for the offence with the lowest punishment, if they differ
punishment: Not applicable — this is a rule for uncertain findings.

verification.source: BNS 2023, Chapter II — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Solitary confinement
bareActText: Whenever any person is convicted of an offence for which under this Sanhita the Court has power to sentence him to rigorous imprisonment, the Court may, by its sentence, order that the offender shall be kept in solitary confinement for any portion or portions of the imprisonment to which he is sentenced, not exceeding three months in the whole, according to the following scale: a time not exceeding one month if the term of imprisonment does not exceed six months; a time not exceeding two months if the term of imprisonment exceeds six months and does not exceed one year; a time not exceeding three months if the term of imprisonment exceeds one year.
plainMeaning: Solitary confinement can only be ordered where the offence allows rigorous imprisonment, and only up to a total of three months, spread according to a scale tied to the length of the sentence: up to 1 month (imprisonment ≤ 6 months), up to 2 months (6 months–1 year), and up to 3 months (over 1 year).
ingredients: The offence must carry power to impose rigorous imprisonment
Solitary confinement is limited to three months in total
Scale: ≤1 month if imprisonment ≤6 months; ≤2 months if 6 months–1 year; ≤3 months if over 1 year
punishment: Not applicable — this is a limited sentencing power.

verification.source: BNS 2023, s.11 — cross-checked against India Code text as reported by PRS India, Drishti Judiciary, and Testbook (Sep 2026).

title: Limit of solitary confinement
bareActText: In executing a sentence of solitary confinement, such confinement shall in no case exceed fourteen days at a time, with intervals between the periods of solitary confinement of not less duration than such periods; and when the imprisonment awarded shall exceed three months, the solitary confinement shall not exceed seven days in any one month of the whole imprisonment awarded, with intervals between the periods of solitary confinement of not less duration than such periods.
plainMeaning: Even when solitary confinement is ordered, it can never run more than 14 days at a stretch, and must be separated by gaps at least as long. For sentences over three months, it is capped at seven days in any single month.
ingredients: Solitary confinement must not exceed 14 days at a time
Intervals between periods must be at least as long as the periods
For imprisonment over three months, no more than 7 days of solitary confinement in any one month
punishment: Not applicable — this caps how solitary confinement is executed.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.74 IPC; retained without change in language.

verification.source: BNS 2023, s.12 — bare Act text matches the verbatim statutory text quoted by Testbook (citing India Code) and confirmed by Drishti Judiciary (Sep 2026).

title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction
bareActText: Whoever, having been convicted of an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII of this Sanhita with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards, shall be guilty of any offence punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term, shall be subject for every such subsequent offence to imprisonment for life, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years. (Refer to the Gazette for the full text.)
plainMeaning: A repeat offender who is convicted again of a serious offence under the specified chapters can face a heavier punishment — up to life imprisonment or up to ten years — because of the prior conviction.
ingredients: A prior conviction under the specified chapters carrying 3 years or more
A later offence of the like kind under those chapters
Enhanced punishment: up to life, or up to ten years
punishment: Enhanced: imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, for the qualifying repeat offence.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.75 IPC on enhanced punishment after a previous conviction.
